name: Scarlet S

lead:
Scarlet S is a fractional radiofrequency (RF) microneedling device. Microneedling punctures the skin with fine needles, and RF versions add heat energy at the needle tips. People have it done in clinics for firmer-looking skin, smoother texture and softened acne scars.
General microneedling is studied for scarring and acne and in combination with minoxidil for hair loss. No studies specific to Scarlet S exist.

paras: A clinician passes the device over numbed skin in a session; several sessions are typical for scars. Redness and swelling follow, then skin improves gradually.
Pain, redness, swelling and temporary marks are common; infection is a concern when done by untrained operators. Choose a licensed provider.

angle.text: People use fractional RF microneedling to tighten skin and soften scars. Results build over several sessions.

lead: Scarlet S is a fractional radiofrequency microneedling device, also called Scarlet RF. Clinics use such devices to improve skin texture, firmness and acne scars.

Microneedling, also known as collagen induction therapy, punctures the skin with tiny sterile needles; it is used for scarring and acne, and combined with minoxidil it has shown better hair loss results than minoxidil alone in some studies.[1] Infection risk rises when it is done in non-medical settings by untrained people, and in 2024 the CDC reported three HIV diagnoses among patients of one New Mexico spa offering vampire facials.[1]
No studies of Scarlet S specifically were found.

paras: Microneedling punctures the skin repeatedly to prompt healing; research continues, and efficacy of combinations such as with platelet-rich plasma remains in question pending studies.[1]
No studies found for Scarlet S.
